articles.title: Docker Desktop is Secretly Hoarding 30GB — Here's How to Reclaim It
articles.excerpt: You open System Settings → General → Storage on your Mac and see the dreaded label: "System Data: 98 GB". You haven't downloaded movies, and your Downloads folder is empty. Yet your 512GB SSD is choki…
articles.body: You open System Settings → General → Storage on your Mac and see the dreaded label: "System Data: 98 GB" . You haven't downloaded movies, and your Downloads folder is empty. Yet your 512GB SSD is choking. If you are a developer on macOS, the primary suspect is almost certainly Docker Desktop . Even with just a few containers or a local Postgres instance, Docker on macOS silently hoards 30GB to 80GB of disk space. Worse: when you delete containers or images inside Docker, macOS doesn't automatically get that disk space back . In this guide, we'll dissect Docker Desktop's storage architecture on macOS, explain why the virtual disk never shrinks on its own, and provide Terminal commands to reclaim your space. 1.
articles.author: Sarmad Hussain

articles.title: How we let AI agents spend money without a blank check
articles.excerpt: If you give an agent an API key on a funded account, you've given it a card. Most APIs are fine with that: they bill per call, and a loop that runs all night shows up on next month's invoice. We could…
articles.body: If you give an agent an API key on a funded account, you've given it a card. Most APIs are fine with that: they bill per call, and a loop that runs all night shows up on next month's invoice. We couldn't ship it that way. SpecStream turns one sentence ("critical vulnerabilities published this month, with the affected product and the fixed version") into a list of matches from the live web, and you pay per match. One badly worded request from an agent can mean thousands of rows nobody wanted. So in our API the key isn't the permission. A price is. Nothing that spends money runs until someone approves a specific price for a specific request, with a ceiling in cents. Here's the whole flow in four calls.

articles.title: AWS Outage One Year Later: Lessons From Every Cloud Failure
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Every major cloud provider has had a serious outage since mid-2025, each from a different cause, so any single provider is a single point of failure. On October 20, 2025, a DNS race condition in…
articles.body: TL;DR Every major cloud provider has had a serious outage since mid-2025, each from a different cause, so any single provider is a single point of failure. On October 20, 2025, a DNS race condition in DynamoDB's automation took the DynamoDB endpoint in AWS us-east-1 offline. The event ran about 15 hours and spread to EC2 instance launches and Network Load Balancers. Google Cloud (June 2025, global), Azure Front Door (October 2025, global), Oracle Cloud US East (Ashburn) (March 2026), and an automated Google Cloud action that suspended a customer's production account (May 2026) each failed in a different layer. Failures hit three blast radii: a zone, a region, or a whole provider. Multi-region on one provider covers the first two.

articles.title: I built a voice-controlled snooker scorekeeper for iPhone
articles.excerpt: I've played snooker for decades, and for just as long I've been annoyed by the same thing: breaking my focus after every shot to tap a scorekeeping app. So I built SnookScore, an iPhone app that keeps…
articles.body: I've played snooker for decades, and for just as long I've been annoyed by the same thing: breaking my focus after every shot to tap a scorekeeping app. So I built SnookScore , an iPhone app that keeps score by voice. Say the ball ("red", "pink", "black"), "another" for a repeat, or "miss" and it tracks the frame for you. Fouls, free balls, the endgame color sequence - the full rule set is handled. The hardest parts The game logic. Snooker scoring has more edge cases than you'd think (foul and a miss, free ball after a snooker, the endgame colors...). Modeling the frame state correctly took the most time. Interpreting voice commands against the current frame state. "Blue" means something different when only the colors remain.

articles.title: AI Voice for Gaming: Creating Dynamic NPC Dialogue
articles.excerpt: Why AI‑Generated Voice is a Game‑Changer for NPCs If you’ve ever played a game where the same three lines repeat for every side‑quest, you know how immersion can crack. Traditional voice‑over pipeline…
articles.body: Why AI‑Generated Voice is a Game‑Changer for NPCs If you’ve ever played a game where the same three lines repeat for every side‑quest, you know how immersion can crack. Traditional voice‑over pipelines are expensive and inflexible: you record a line, lock it in, and any change means a new studio session. Enter modern text‑to‑speech (TTS) and voice‑cloning. With a high‑quality neural model you can generate any line on the fly, match a character’s personality, and even let players shape how an NPC sounds. The result? Dynamic dialogue that reacts to player choices, procedural quests, and emergent storytelling—all without a massive voice‑over budget. In this article I’ll walk through the practical steps to plug an AI voice service into a game, using ElevenLabs as the backbone.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.

articles.body: A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it. The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12.

articles.title: Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal
articles.excerpt: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander.
articles.body: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis. Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world. The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.
